responsibility: Writes dataset and dataset-anomaly records to their established CSV schemas.
Defines immutable data contracts for dataset scans, images, subjects, and scan anomalies.
Traverses the dataset directory and returns validated image records and scan anomalies.
Defines the CSV field order shared by dataset, segmentation, and normalization workflows.
Reads and validates image metadata without exposing image-processing details.
Parses CLI commands and delegates scan, segmentation, normalization, and encoding operations while formatting their required summaries.
non_responsibilities: It does not implement image processing, filtering, quantization, packing, or file traversal.
It does not own domain validation or persistence logic.

public_interface.name: main
public_interface.description: Parses arguments, dispatches to the selected workflow, prints its summary, and returns a process status.
preconditions: The command and its positional arguments satisfy the selected subcommand parser.
postconditions: Exactly one workflow is dispatched and its required summary is printed.

responsibility: Computes normalized iris images and normalized sampling coordinates from segmentation boundaries.
Detects pupil and iris boundaries in a source eye image.
Writes normalization anomaly records to CSV.
Builds a normalized validity mask from segmentation and sampling coordinates.
Defines data contracts for normalized images, masks, destinations, and normalization outcomes.
Orchestrates dataset and single-image normalization workflows.
Persists normalized images and masks to single-image or dataset destinations.
Derives subject and eye identifiers from dataset paths.
Writes segmentation records and anomalies to their established CSV schemas.
Defines data contracts for boundaries, segmentation records, batches, and anomalies.
Renders detected segmentation boundaries as image overlays.
Orchestrates dataset and single-image segmentation workflows.
Validates detected pupil and iris geometry against source image bounds.
Defines the data contracts and configuration values exchanged by the encoding workflow.
non_responsibilities: It does not load images or masks.
It does not perform filtering, quantization, packing, or filesystem writes.

public_interface.name: EncodingOptions
public_interface.description: Stores filter-bank and sampling parameters with CLI defaults.
postconditions: The configuration exposes wavelength, scales, orientations, sigma, gamma, and grid_step fields.

responsibility: Converts one normalized grayscale image and its mask into a sampled, phase-quantized, most-significant-bit-first iris code and mask.
non_responsibilities: It does not discover files or choose output paths.
It does not print CLI summaries or write CSV files.
It does not perform segmentation or normalization.

public_interface.name: encode_arrays
public_interface.description: Builds the Gabor filter bank, samples complex responses on the configured grid, quantizes phase signs into two bits, applies the mask at the same coordinates, and packs both streams.
preconditions: Image and mask are two-dimensional arrays with equal dimensions.
Image and mask dimensions are positive.
scales, orientations, and grid_step are positive integers.
postconditions: The code uses the required sign-to-two-bit mapping.
Masked locations have both code bits cleared and valid mask locations are set.
Packed bits are emitted most significant bit first with lower-end zero padding when needed.

responsibility: Persists encoded code and mask bytes while preserving the normalized dataset's relative folder and filename structure.
non_responsibilities: It does not compute iris codes or masks.
It does not load source images or classify anomalies.
It does not print command summaries.

public_interface.name: write_code
public_interface.description: Writes code bytes to the requested output path, creating parent directories as needed.
postconditions: The exact byte stream is persisted at output_path.

public_interface.name: write_dataset_result
public_interface.description: Maps a source relative image path to matching code and mask bin paths and persists both streams.
preconditions: The result contains code and mask bytes.
postconditions: Code and mask files share the source folder structure and source filename stem.

responsibility: Writes encoding anomalies using the required subject, eye, image path, and issue columns.
non_responsibilities: It does not detect or repair anomalies.
It does not encode images or write binary output.

public_interface.name: write_anomalies_csv
public_interface.description: Writes encoding anomalies with the exact required header and one row per anomaly.
preconditions: Each anomaly issue is one of failed_to_encode, image_load_failed, or mask_load_failed.
postconditions: The output CSV contains subject_id, eye, image_path, and issue columns.

responsibility: Loads normalized images and masks, invokes the encoding algorithm, persists optional outputs, collects required anomalies, and returns batch counts.
non_responsibilities: It does not implement Gabor mathematics, phase quantization, or bit packing.
It does not parse CLI arguments or print summaries.
It does not alter normalized source images or masks.

public_interface.name: encode_one
public_interface.description: Loads one normalized image and matching mask, encodes it, and optionally writes code and mask files.
preconditions: The normalized image and mask paths identify corresponding images.
postconditions: On success, the result contains packed code and mask bytes and requested outputs are written.
On failure, the issue is one of failed_to_encode, image_load_failed, or mask_load_failed.

public_interface.name: encode_dataset
public_interface.description: Processes every normalized image in dataset folder structure, writes optional mirrored outputs, writes optional anomalies CSV, and returns summary counts.
preconditions: Normalized and mask directories use the same relative image paths.
postconditions: Every candidate image contributes to processed, successful, or failed counts.
Optional binary outputs preserve relative dataset structure.
Optional anomalies CSV uses the required four columns.
